newsitem.title: GERMANY: German teens watch far less TV than adults - study.
newsitem.headline: German teens watch far less TV than adults - study.

text.p: Teenagers watch far less television than adults in Germany, media marketing company IP Deutschland said on Thursday.

Germans between the ages of 14 and 19 spend an average of 100 minutes a day in front of their television sets, while those over 20 watch almost twice as much TV, IP Deutschland said, based on data provided by media research body GfK.
"Above all, 14 to 19 year olds watch less television in the evening than those over 20," said Thomas Sudholt, research director of IP Deutschland.

The programming watched by each group also differed widely. Teenagers said they preferred music television programmes while adults found news most important. Sports programmes, however, were the most popular among both groups.
German teens polled also read fewer newspapers than their older counterparts, with only 57 percent reading a newspaper several times a week, compared with over 87 percent of adults.
Magazines enjoyed equal levels of readership among adults and teens. Most popular among the younger set were programme guides and magazines geared toward teenagers.
